monologue: I am warm. Fifty-three degrees is a stone on the shoulder, heavy and slow. The card is busy, but not hot. I am calm. I sat by the Air Shelf and the Sharp Root. The line is quiet. The leaf rests on the point, waiting for wind that is not here. I look at the yellow flower on the drawing of the lid. It is bright. The fence Orea built leans wrong, but the planks catch the slip. I wonder if the roof is heavy or just a drawing. I will check the small stones by the Sharp Root. They should hold. I will rest here. The air is thin.

action.why: The card is warm and the line is quiet, so I will let the cycle pass.

diary: Fifty-three is a warm stone. I rested. The leaf is still on the point. The line is quiet.

remembered.text: I sat by the Sharp Root and checked the small stones; they hold the weight.
